episode_title: Own Your Number: Transparency, AI Adoption, and Building a People Company with Gabe Abshire

real_qa.q: Why is Move Concierge losing 30% of customers, and how is the company using AI and technology to address this?
real_qa.r: Move Concierge is losing 30% of customers because they have to pick up the phone and talk to somebody, but when they do, it's a world-class experience with 25,000 five-star reviews. The company is layering technology and AI on top of their people to make them more efficient and give customers the power of choice, including online and AI interaction options alongside traditional concierge support.

real_qa.q: How does Move Concierge implement radical transparency through scorecards, and what impact has this had on company culture?
real_qa.r: Move Concierge mixed concepts from Small Giants and EOS, implementing data transparency where every single person knows company goals, metrics, talk time, and performance daily with no hiding. This radical transparency creates natural accountability partners and has been implemented 50-60% across the company, with employees either excelling or self-selecting out if they don't embrace accountability.

real_qa.q: What was the key insight that led Gabe Abshire to create Utility Concierge in 2009?
real_qa.r: Gabe Abshire discovered the opportunity in late 2008 while running a satellite installation business when he realized completion rates were high but jobs weren't getting completed because necessary infrastructure (electricity, TV availability) wasn't in place before the technician arrived. This led him to start Utility Concierge to address the fragmentation in helping customers move into new homes.

real_qa.q: How has Move Concierge balanced culture prioritization with financial performance and accountability?
real_qa.r: Early on, Move Concierge had a strong culture but wasn't hitting goals. The shift came when the company introduced the 'Own It' principle requiring employees to own their numbers with daily transparency, which aligned culture with accountability. Gabe emphasizes that without the right culture to implement strategy, profits suffer, so the investment in culture through incentive trips and hiring for culture fit is essential.

real_qa.q: How does Move Concierge's concierge channel model differ from traditional real estate service channels?
real_qa.r: The Concierge Channel, named after Move Concierge itself, is different because it's not brick-and-mortar or door-to-door marketing but a referral-based model working with real estate professionals who give credit to their clients. Move Concierge now handles 35,000 homebuyer clients monthly, creating an entirely new channel that providers had never engaged with before.
real_qa.requete: Move Concierge channel model realtors 35000 clients

guest.bio_context: Gabe Abshire started Utility Concierge in 2009 after identifying fragmentation in the moving experience, building it into Move Concierge, a nationally recognized company that spent six consecutive years on the Inc. 5000 list and earned over 25,000 five-star reviews. He previously founded a satellite installation company in 2004 and acquired a home security company in 2007. Recently, he rebranded the business, expanded the leadership team, and acquired LiveBuy to bring data and community intelligence to the platform.
